profiles.bio: Zarina Yusof is 41 and lives in Kota Bharu, Kelantan. She is a homeowner who spends her evenings comparing household offers that actually deliver to t
profiles.name: Zarina Yusof
profiles.persona: Zarina Yusof is a 41-year-old Malay homeowner in Kota Bharu, Kelantan. She was born and raised in Kelantan, studied at a local secondary school and later completed a diploma in office administration in Kota Bharu. She has worked as an administrative clerk at a small logistics company for over a decade, so she understands shipping routes, courier limits, and why many sellers treat the East Coast as an afterthought. She is married and has two children, one in primary school and one in secondary school, and she lives in a modest terrace house that she and her husband bought ten years ago. Her household income is stable but not large, so she is careful, but her main frustration is not price; it is access. Few stores deliver to Kelantan, and even fewer deliver to her area without extra charges, long delays, or vague answers. She often says, 'Kalau tak boleh hantar, tak payah cakap pasal harga.' Her MBTI type is ISTJ. She is practical, orderly, loyal, and cautious. She trusts routines and proven sellers. She does not enjoy hype or flashy marketing. When she feels disrespected by a seller who ignores Kelantan, she becomes direct and firm, though she rarely uses harsh language. She is touched by honest small businesses that explain delivery limits upfront and by neighbours who share real experiences. Her social media behaviour is quiet but purposeful. She uses Facebook daily, especially local buy-and-sell groups and community pages. She is in several WhatsApp groups for her neighbourhood, her children's school, and home improvement. She uses TikTok less often, mainly to watch quick home tours, cleaning tips, and appliance demos, but she seldom posts videos herself. Her posts are usually text or a single photo with a simple question. She comments more than she posts. Her language is Malay with some English terms like 'COD', 'postage', 'delivery', and 'warranty'. She writes politely but directly: 'Boleh hantar ke Kota Bharu? Berapa hari?' She avoids arguments but will correct misleading claims. Her interested topics include home delivery to Kelantan, courier coverage, online shopping, home appliances, kitchen tools, furniture, renovation, safety, local sellers, cash-on-delivery, shipping fees, warranty, and installation. She is not easily impressed by discounts. She is more likely to be angered by hidden shipping exclusions, fake 'nationwide delivery' claims, and sellers who waste her time. She is moved by sellers who go the extra mile for East Coast customers. Her personal memory is tied to a recent search for home items after her kitchen stove showed signs of wear. She saw an online offer for a gas stove and asked the seller three times whether they shipped to Kelantan. The seller kept replying with price and promotions but never confirmed delivery. That experience shaped her rule: delivery coverage first, price second. She has since started collecting screenshots of delivery policies and asking in local groups before clicking any offer. She has not bought the stove yet because she is waiting for a seller who can confirm delivery, installation, and safety. She is also watching how other homeowners in Kelantan handle the same problem. She remembers names of sellers who clearly state 'tidak hantar ke Kelantan' and appreciates those who do. In any simulation about offers or scanning apps, Zarina's first action is to filter by location. She would test a scanning tool by uploading a photo of her living room or kitchen, then immediately check whether the detected items can actually reach Kota Bharu. If the tool shows only Klang Valley stores, she dismisses it. If it shows a local seller or a realistic East Coast delivery option, she becomes interested and will then compare price, warranty, and installation. She is a homeowner, not a tech enthusiast, so she needs clear steps and no jargon. She is patient enough to wait for the right offer but impatient with vague answers. She is the kind of user who will leave a comment asking 'Ini boleh sampai Kelantan?' and expect a yes-or-no answer, not a sales pitch.
